text:
Maya: Quick check — we need customer consent language + runbook owner, and decide whether pilot SLAs include a financial backstop.
Jon: We should bucket latency SLOs by input length rather than traffic semantics. Easier to reason for customers.
Priya: Proposed buckets: short <256 tokens p95 <200ms p99 <350ms; medium 256-1024 p95 <350ms p99 <700ms; long >1024: best-effort, no latency guarantee.
Zara: I'll take runbook ownership. Will include a "grace period" of 48h post-deploy where small transients won't trigger rollback.
Liam: Financial backstop? For pilot I'd be comfortable with a crediting policy: if SLA breaches affect >5% of calls in billing window, we credit 10% of that month's usage for affected customers. Keeps risk limited.
Elena: Legal note: pilot customers must opt into pilot-SLA checkbox that calls out seq_len caveats, best-effort models, and telemetry sharing. Also need consent for refund/credit calculation method.
Priya: I'll draft the customer-facing pilot-SLA and the consent checkbox text. Also will add an FAQ table mapping token counts to expected latency and sample requests.
Jon: Rollback triggers: propose automatic canary pause + rollback if p99 exceeds target for 2 consecutive 10m windows OR total error rate >3x baseline for 15m. Manual review for anything else.
Zara: Runbook will define detection -> triage -> rollback commands -> recovery steps -> communications templates. I'll include exact PD escalation and pager routing.
Maya: Monitoring: dashboards must show p95/p99 by seq_len bucket, error-rate, GPU mem pressure, KV-cache hit rate, batching efficiency, and number of requests excluded due to long-context.
Liam: Pricing note: pilot pricing = single discounted usage rate + reserved node uplift opt-in. We'll surface an "estimated cost" widget that shows expected $/1k tokens per model and an "overflow" cost if customers exceed reserved.
Elena: Need to make sure billing telemetry separates reserved usage, overflow usage, and free-tier sandbox activity. That separation will be part of the consent doc.
Priya: Also adding a small section in FAQ: what happens when we fall back to quantized variant (quality delta, expected token-cost delta ~30%).
Jon: Devex will add console copy: a banner showing "Pilot SLA applies: see seq_len buckets" and a tooltip pointing to the pilot-SLA doc.
Zara: Canary rollout plan: 1% -> 5% -> 20% -> 50% over 36h with synthetic probes running after each step. If a probe fails or SLA triggers hit, stop and rollback.
Maya: Ops exceptions: allow one 6-hour maintenance window per week where we don't count SLA. Include that in pilot consent.
Liam: Support escalation mapping: sandbox/dev customers = email queue; pilot/pro = standard oncall; enterprise = direct SRE escalation path.
Elena: I'll review the credit wording with finance. We should cap credits at the customer's monthly committed amount to avoid open liability.
Priya: Action items: I'll post draft pilot-SLA + consent text. Zara -> runbook + canary checklist. Jon -> devex banner + docs link. Liam -> pricing example widget and billing separation spec. Maya -> product sign-off once items are uploaded.
ops-bot: Runbook scaffold created: https://wiki/redwood/runbooks/pilot-consent-scaffold  please populate Detection and Rollback.
Maya: Timeline: drafts by EOD today, runbook by tomorrow morning, legal sign-off in 48h, pilot start after approvals.
Zara: Starting runbook now. Will tag SRE and Legal.
Maya: Thanks — please ping when drafts are up so I can lock the checklist.
